title: The Deadliest Sea Animal From Every Single Period
format: 16:9 long-form, 854x480 @30fps source, 41m20s, single narrator VO, YouTube chapters per period

title_pattern.template: The Deadliest [Category] From Every Single [Time Unit / Place]
title_pattern.type: superlative x exhaustive-set ranking ('one winner per bucket' timeline list)
title_pattern.notes: Two promises in one line: a superlative (deadliest) and completeness ('every single' period). The completeness phrase implies a long binge-able list and signals a chronological escalation. Category 'sea animal' borrows thalassophobia appeal. No number, no caps, no emoji; plain title case. The same channel template recurs (deadliest/largest X from every era).
variants_to_try: The Deadliest Predator From Every Single Ice Age
The Largest Flying Animal From Every Single Period
The Worst Place To Be Born In Every Single Century
The Most Dangerous Ocean Zone At Every Single Depth

thumbnail.composition: Radial 'surrounded' composition: a tiny scuba diver silhouette at bottom-centre with a cone of torchlight shining up into black-navy water; seven period champions (Endoceras orthocone squid top-centre, ichthyosaur, Basilosaurus-like whale, Edestus scissor-jaw shark, megalodon, a second shark, a small sea-scorpion/arthropod) ring the diver, all faces aimed at him. Painterly paleoart, no frame borders.
thumbnail.colours: Near-monochrome deep navy/teal, one bright cyan light cone in the centre; creatures desaturated blue-grey and brown with small accents (pinkish tentacles, white teeth). Dark vignette edges.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Human is ~1/10 the height of each monster; the lone lit diver vs a wall of looming toothy faces in the dark is the whole premise (deadliest of every period, all at once).
thumbnail.why_it_works: Thalassophobia in one glance: darkness + you-are-the-diver POV + many grinning predators. The lineup implies the list format (one beast per period) without text. Light cone pulls the eye to the human first, then outward to each monster, creating a scanning loop. Readable at phone size because faces and teeth are large and high-contrast against the dark.

hook.verbatim_0_10s: One of the toughest and realest bars ever dropped by an honorary paleontologist is: no matter how bad things get on land, never get into the water.
hook.first_5s: One of the toughest and realest bars ever dropped by an honorary paleontologist is no matter how bad...
hook.device: Borrowed maxim / cold-open quote from a recognizable TV wildlife presenter (archival talking-head clip, likely Nigel Marven of 'Chased by Sea Monsters'), framed with slang ('realest bars') and then burned in as big kinetic caption with the last line in red. Followed at 0:17-0:35 by a relatable personal-choice comparison (tiger/lion vs shark/croc; 'drop me anywhere on land rather than water') and at 0:53-1:10 by the explicit question that frames the whole video: if you were sent back through every period, what is the worst thing you could swim into?
hook.notes: Hook lands the rule (land < sea) in 10 s, validates it with a gut-level 'would you rather', then turns it into a time-travel POV question. First chapter card at 1:17, so the cold open is ~77 s, ~3% of runtime.

structure_summary: Chronological countdown-by-era (12 rounds) with escalating size. Each round reuses the same template: (1) bridge from previous period's extinction/climate event, (2) big chapter title card with timeline ruler, (3) context: world map + which group rose, (4) famous foil or runner-up named, (5) winner reveal with name title, (6) stat card (taxonomy box + body length/weight vs human/diver silhouette), (7) weapons segment: jaws/teeth/claws with one big number (bite force in Newtons) compared to a modern animal, (8) relatable scale comparisons (giraffe, NBA player, sperm whale, NFL player, tallest human), (9) range/habitat + 'you would not survive' joke, (10) cliffhanger bridge: 'somehow worse things were on the horizon'. Rounds lengthen as animals get famous (Cambrian 2.5 min, Triassic 5 min, Neogene 4.6 min). Ends with a 20 s present-day punchline (humans are the deadliest).

beats.summary: Archival presenter clip + burned-in maxim: never get in the water.
Would-you-rather: tiger or lion on land vs shark or crocodile in water; 'drop me on land any day'.
Rule holds through deep time: every era's sea predators were worse than land ones, and there were many of them.
POV time-travel question: if sent through every period since the Cambrian, what is the worst thing you could swim into? Lowered expectations for the Cambrian ('not kraken sizes yet').
CAMBRIAN card; tiny life; famous Anomalocaris introduced as the expected answer with size (Chihuahua weight) and appendages.
'In reality this weird shrimp was not the real nightmare': Omnidens reveal, mouth-on-the-belly gross detail ('wait for it'), 1.5 m apex; framed as the smallest contender, 'only bigger from here'.
ORDOVICIAN card ('Release the Kraken!'); Panthalassic map; cephalopods' golden age, live squid/nautilus footage.

Endoceras: cone shell roles (icon roundels), 5.7 m = giraffe height, rumoured 9 m shell, sticky tentacles, beak, poor eyes/good smell; reassurance twist ('only 100 kg, would not eat us. Likely.') and cliffhanger 'rather deal with this than what's next'.
Ice age bridge, SILURIAN card; eurypterids rise; not true scorpions; stinger telsons longer than knives.
Jaekelopterus: 2.6 m beats tallest NBA player, 200+ kg, arm-length pincers, gnathobases, rudder telson ('you think you could outrun it - fatal belief'), first freshwater entry.
DEVONIAN card, '419 million years ago', THE AGE OF FISH title; placoderm class chart.

Dunkleosteus: addresses the size-downgrade controversy head-on ('the allegations are true... the Dunk has not sunk'), guillotine bone plates, suction, 7,495 N vs jaguar, 4.1 m = great white but 1.7 t, armour 25x knight armour, fossil map.
CARBONIFEROUS card; golden age of sharks, 45 families; Eugeneodontida tooth whorls.
Edestus: 6.7 m scissor-tooth shark, two-gear jaw hypothesis with diagrams, ~2,000 N, 'no beaches' meme, shallow tropical habitat; bridge 'its family was about to get more overpowered'.

PERMIAN: Parahelicoprion/Helicoprion as 'the Megalodon of the Paleozoic', 7-13 m (rumoured 30 m, Jaws 'bigger boat' gag), buzzsaw tooth whorl half your body, Pangaea range, possible diet card; 'stay away from all oceans'.
Great Dying bridge; TRIASSIC card; ichthyosaurs, dolphin convergence.

Ichthyotitan: 25 m > sperm whale, 35-80 t, possible 35 m Aust specimen; teeth caveat ('we haven't found teeth') with backup picks Shastasaurus and Thalattoarchon - honest uncertainty used as mini-ranking; volcanic extinction bridge.

JURASSIC: pliosaurs; 'Predator X'; 2023 Kimmeridge specimen 14.4 m (3x great white), skull longer than an NFL player, 42,000 N, trihedral teeth, bite-straight-down kill ('Nighty night. Hasta luego. Sayonara.'), generalist, complete package; 'somehow worse things were on the horizon'.

CRETACEOUS: Mosasaurus hoffmannii 'swimming T. rex', 12 m 10+ t, quadrate 150% bigger = Robert Wadlow analogy, crush+slice teeth, speed, binocular vision; Tylosaurus rival coin-flip; asteroid ends both.

PALEOGENE: Basilosaurus, whale mistaken for lizard, 20 m 15 t, differentiated teeth that chew, croc-level bite, Dorudon in stomachs, no melon but directional hearing ('even in the abyss it knew where you were'); mid-Eocene extinction opens the throne.

NEOGENE: Megalodon 'peak of the thalassophobia mountain'; keeps getting bigger (Shimada: 24 m, 80-104 t = 2x sperm whale), newer elongated body plan, 276 teeth, 182,000 N = axe at 110 mph, whale bite marks, Livyatan rival ('what I want for Christmas'), found everywhere ('if you swam, you were screwed'), extinct 3.58 Mya.
Present period: unfair to rank yet, but humans would top the list; sign-off 'until next time on Extinct Zoo'.

pacing.shot_length_method: frame-difference on 2 s samples: ~540-600 visual changes in 2480 s (=4.1-4.6 s); undercounts sub-2 s cuts, but nearly every still also carries Ken Burns motion so the screen is never static
pacing.visual_change_profile: Lower cut rate than shorts (4-5 s), compensated by constant slow motion and overlays (cards, counters, silhouettes) every 15-30 s
pacing.rehook_interval_s: ~20-40 s: each round inserts a number reveal, a scale comparison, a joke, or a 'but that's not even the craziest part' turn

techniques_worth_copying: Exhaustive-set superlative format: one winner per bucket in chronological order, so escalation (size goes up every round) is built into the structure and every chapter ends with 'worse is coming'.
Famous-foil subversion at the start of each round: name the animal viewers expect (Anomalocaris), then 'in reality the real nightmare was...' a lesser-known one.
Recurring branded chapter card: huge condensed title, playful bracketed subtitle ('Release the Kraken!'), MYA range and a geologic timeline ruler showing progress through the video.

Stat card template reused every round: beige graph-paper card, taxonomy box (CLASS/ORDER/FAMILY/GENUS), human/diver silhouette and familiar object silhouette for scale, body-length bar with metric + imperial.
Every big number is translated into a familiar comparison: giraffe, tallest NBA player, great white, sperm whale, NFL player, Robert Wadlow, knight armour, axe at 110 mph, jaguar bite.
Count-up kinetic numbers for bite force in Newtons and percentages, split-screen versus a modern animal.
Second-person POV threat framing ('you would be in two pieces', 'if you swam, you were screwed', 'you might think you could outrun it') keeps a survival stakes thread across 40 minutes.
Honest uncertainty turned into content: size-downgrade controversy addressed head-on, missing-teeth caveat answered with backup picks, rumoured giant specimens as 'it gets crazier'.
Extinction events as transitions: each round's ending doubles as the next round's setup, which removes dead air between chapters.
Light comedic punctuation every 1-2 minutes (puns 'the Dunk has not sunk', meme inserts, 'Nighty night. Hasta luego. Sayonara.', Christmas wish for a Meg vs Livyatan fossil).
Thumbnail: lone lit diver encircled by every champion in the dark; no text, all faces pointed at the viewer surrogate.

code_only_remake_needs.summary: Structure, cards, charts, maps and kinetic type are fully reproducible in Remotion/SVG. What the original leans on and we cannot use is licensed CGI clips (Prehistoric Planet, Life on Our Planet, etc.), credited paleoart and archival interviews; those must be replaced by a consistent original vector creature style.
assets: Original SVG creature library (~15 species) in one flat or silhouette-plus-rim-light style, each with parts rigged for simple loops: tail sway, jaw open/close, tentacle wave, fin flap
Layered parallax underwater backgrounds per era (gradient water, light shafts, particulate, kelp/reef silhouettes, seafloor), tinted per period
Human/diver, giraffe, NBA player, sperm whale, great white, school bus silhouettes for scale
Simplified paleogeographic globe/flat maps per period (SVG continents) with pulsing location pins
Icon set: swim, balance, shield, intimidation, lock, eye, ear, tooth
components: ChapterTitleCard: huge condensed type with tracking-in, bracketed italic subtitle, MYA range, animated geologic timeline ruler with active period highlight
StatCard: graph-paper card, creature + scale silhouettes, length bar with metric/imperial, taxonomy table, sequential icon highlights
ScaleCompare: before/after silhouettes and height lineup charts
NumberCounter: bite force / percentage count-up with split-screen modern comparison
AnatomyDiagram: line-art callouts that draw on (stroke-dashoffset) for jaws, tooth whorls, appendages
KenBurns wrapper for every scene so nothing is ever static; crossfade and light-flash transitions
Kinetic caption burn-in for the hook line with a red emphasis line
code_only_remake_needs.audio: ~200 wpm single narrator (Kokoro/Piper on CPU), low ambient underwater drone bed, sub-bass hits on number reveals and title cards
code_only_remake_needs.runtime_notes: 41 min is too long for a pilot; the template compresses well to 8-12 min with 6-8 rounds, or a shorts series (one period per 50-60 s short using the same cards).
